text:
max: hi team — i'm wrapping up my first PR for notifications-service. quick onboarding questions: 1) do we branch from main or from a staging branch for small features? 2) i accidentally checked in some compiled JS under build/ — should i remove that? 3) any tips for getting a fast review?

yun: welcome Max! :wave: short answers: branch from main for small, single-author work. staging/ or release/* are for coordinated rollouts. compiled assets like build/ should NOT be committed. remove them and add to .gitignore.

rachael: for removing compiled stuff, this is the workflow I use:
```bash
# remove generated files from git but keep locally
git rm -r --cached build/ || true
# add to .gitignore if missing
echo "build/" >> .gitignore
git add .gitignore
git commit -m "chore(notifications): remove generated build artifacts from repo"
```
then force-push the branch. CI will re-run builds as needed.

max: thanks — i have some lint errors too. are hooks enforced?

yun: we have Husky pre-commit hooks but they sometimes skip (windows, etc). run `yarn format && yarn lint` locally. If lint autofix touches many files, split that into a separate formatting PR to keep reviews focused.

ops-bot: ops-bot: NOTE: CODEOWNERS requires @team-notifications approval for anything under services/notifications/*

rachael: reviewers: add one from CODEOWNERS and one cross-functional (product or SRE) if the change affects behavior or retries. In the PR body include: Summary, Why, Testing steps, and any rollout notes. For UI/UX add screenshots or gif.

max: what's our commit message style? conventional commits?

yun: yes-ish. we prefer conventional commits with a ticket: `type(scope): short summary (TICKET-123)`. Example: `fix(notifications): dedupe retry path (NOTIF-123)`. Include a short body: Why/Testing/Notes. We squash-&-merge by default.

max: one more: i'm modifying a proto and the generated go file was flagged in CI. Should I commit the generated file?

rachael: do NOT commit generated artifacts (proto/gen/*) unless explicitly asked. Instead commit the proto source, run `make gen` locally to verify, and ensure CI's generated output matches. If CI shows a mismatch, regenerate and only commit the source proto changes.

max: got it. also, how small should a PR be? i've got ~400 lines changed across a couple of files.

yun: guideline: if a reviewer can reasonably read it in ~20 minutes it's fine. If it spans multiple services or requires mental-model changes, split. For ~400 LOC that's usually okay if it's focused and tests are present. Add an explicit checklist in the PR: what to run locally, and sample inputs.

ci-bot: ci-bot: build #5222  FAILED  gofmt/proto-gen mismatch in proto/gen/notifications.pb.go

max: that failure is what i saw. i regenerated locally and the file diffs are only generated changes — how do i avoid committing them?

rachael: after regenerating, discard the generated files from the index and only stage the proto source: 
```bash
# regenerate
make gen
# reset generated files to upstream so they don't appear in commit
git checkout origin/main -- proto/gen/* || true
# stage proto sources only
git add path/to/protos/*.proto
git commit -m "feat(notifications): add new event proto (NOTIF-123)"
```
Force-push the cleaned branch. CI will run gen and succeed if your proto is correct.

yun: quick review tip: add a short section in the PR body "Reviewer checklist" with 3 bullets: run tests, check logs for X, confirm no behavioural regressions. That speeds up approvals.

max: perfect — i'll clean up the generated files, run format/lint/tests, add a Reviewer checklist and tag @team-notifications. can someone take a quick look after CI is green?

yun: i can spare 20m after lunch to review.

rachael: same — ping me once CI is green. we usually merge after 1 code-owner approval + green CI.

max: thanks so much, this cleared up a lot :pray: will update and ping here when ready.
